records.arabic: بن عبد المنذر الأنصاري ذكر بن سعد أنه ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال بن حبان في ثقات التابعين روى عن عمر ويقال أن له رؤية وساق بن منده ذلك بسند صحيح ومات بعد المائة وروى له أبو داود حديثا من طريق الحسين بن السائب بن أبي لبابة عن أبيه ذكره تعليقا
records.english: ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir al-Anṣārī. Ibn Saʿd mentioned that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Ibn Hibban said in al-Thiqat al-Tabi'in that he transmitted from Umar, and it is said that he saw the Prophet. Ibn Mandah cited this with a sound chain. He died after the year one hundred. Abu Dawud transmitted a hadith of his by way of al-Husayn ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Abi Lubabah, from his father, citing it without a complete chain.

names.arabic: السائب بن أبي لبابة بن عبد المنذر الأنصاري
الحسين بن السائب بن أبي لبابة
names.english: al-Husayn ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Abi Lubabah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن ربيعة القرشي العامري قال بن ماكولا شهد فتح مصر يقال أنه رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان يلي الشرطة بمصر لمسلمة بن مخلد وكان من جبناء قريش وفي كلام بن يونس أنه ولي القضاء والشرطة بمصر وذكر غيره أن مسلمة ولاه بعد سليم بن عتر ثم عزله بعد يسير لأنه بلغه أنه قال لا ينبغي للقاضي أن يأتي الأمير بل ينبغي للأمير أن يأتي القاضي فعزله وولي عابسا ولم يذكر الكندي في قضاة مصر بين سليم وعابس أحدا وذكر أيضا أنه هو الذي جاء بنعي خارجة بن حذافة لما قتل بمصر
records.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah al-Qurashī al-ʿĀmirī. Ibn Mākūlā said that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt. It is said that he saw the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He commanded the police in Egypt for Maslamah ibn Mukhallad and was one of the cowards of Quraysh. Ibn Yunus's account states that he held both the judgeship and command of the police in Egypt. Someone else mentioned that Maslamah appointed him after Sulaym ibn Itr, then dismissed him shortly afterward because word reached him that al-Sa'ib had said, ‘The judge should not go to the governor; rather, the governor should go to the judge.’ Maslamah dismissed him and appointed Abis. Al-Kindi did not list anyone between Sulaym and Abis among the judges of Egypt. It is also mentioned that al-Sa'ib was the man who brought news of Kharijah ibn Hudhafah's death after he was killed in Egypt.

names.arabic: السائب بن هشام بن عمرو بن ربيعة القرشي العامري

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري من بني عمرو بن عوف ذكر بن سعد أنه ولد على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى عن عمر بن الخطاب وتوفي آخر خلافة عبد الملك
records.english: al-Anṣārī, of the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. Ibn Saʿd mentioned that he was born during the lifetime of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. He transmitted from Umar ibn al-Khattab and died near the end of Abd al-Malik's caliphate.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: يسار بن سبع المزني ويقال الجهني قال بن عساكر ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم ساق بسنده إلى مساور بن شهاب بن مسرور بن مساور بن سعد بن أبي الغادية حدثني أبي عن أبيه مسرور بن مساور عن جده سعد بن أبي الغادية عن أبيه قال فقد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا الغادية في الصلاة فأقبل فقال ما خلفك فقال ولد لي مولود قال هل سميته قال لا قال فجيء به فجاء به فمسح على رأسه بيده وسماه سعدا
records.english: Yasār ibn Sabaʿ al-Muzanī, also said to be al-Juhanī. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, then gave a chain to Musawir ibn Shihab ibn Masrur ibn Musawir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi al-Ghadiyah, who said: ‘My father related to me, from his father Masrur ibn Musawir, from his grandfather Sa'd ibn Abi al-Ghadiyah, from his father, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم noticed Abu al-Ghadiyah's absence from the prayer. When he arrived, the Prophet asked, “What kept you?” He replied, “A child was born to me.” He asked, “Have you named him?” Abu al-Ghadiyah said, “No.” He said, “Bring him.” He brought the child, and the Prophet stroked his head with his hand and named him Sa'd.’

names.arabic: مساور بن شهاب بن مسرور بن مساور بن سعد بن أبي الغادية
names.english: Musawir ibn Shihab ibn Masrur ibn Musawir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi al-Ghadiyah

records.arabic: بن الجدع استشهد أبوه بالطائف وروى سيف في الفتوح عن عبد الله بن سعيد بن ثابت بن الجدع حديثا
records.english: ibn al-Jadhaʿ. His father was martyred at al-Ṭāʾif, and Sayf transmitted in al-Futūḥ from Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Thabit ibn al-Jadaʿ.

names.arabic: عبد الله بن سعيد بن ثابت بن الجدع
names.english: Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Thabit ibn al-Jadaʿ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن نوفل بن عبد المطلب الهاشمي مات أبوه سنة خمس عشرة كما سبق ترجمته وكان سعيد فقيها قاله الزبير بن بكار وهو جد يزيد بن عبد الملك النوفلي لأمه أم عبد الله
records.english: ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī. His father died in the year five and ten, making fifteen, as stated in his notice above. Sa'id was a jurist, according to al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar. Through his daughter Umm Abd Allah, he was the maternal grandfather of Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik al-Nawfali.

names.arabic: سعيد بن الحارث بن نوفل بن عبد المطلب الهاشمي

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أبي وقاص الزهري له ذكر في مقتل علي وأنه نعاه إلى أهل الحجاز وروى الطبراني بسند له عن إسماعيل بن راشد أنه الذي ذهب بنعي علي من معاوية إلى عمرو بن العاص قلت ذكرته في هذا القسم لأن أباه مات كافرا ولعله مات قبل الفتح فإني لم أجد له ذكرا في شيء من كتب الأنساب ولا التواريخ ولا المغازي فهذا أن لم يكن له صحبة فهو أهل هذا القسم والله أعلم
records.english: ibn Abī Waqqāṣ al-Zuhrī. He is mentioned in the account of ʿAlī’s killing and as having announced his death to the people of the Hijaz. Al-Tabarani transmitted with a chain from Isma'il ibn Rashid that Sufyan was the man who carried word of Ali's death from Mu'awiyah to Amr ibn al-As. I say: I have included him in this section because his father died an unbeliever and may have died before the Conquest. I found no mention of him in any work of genealogy, history, or military campaigns. Thus, if he did not have companionship, he belongs in this section. والله أعلم.

names.arabic: سفيان بن عبد شمس بن أبي وقاص الزهري

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أبان بن سلمة بن حارثة بن فهم الفهمي لأبيه صحبة وله رؤية وقتل ولده خفينة بن قيس بن سلمة بن طريف مع الحسين بن علي يوم الطف
records.english: ibn Abān ibn Salamah ibn Ḥārithah ibn Fahm al-Fahmī. His father had companionship. He also saw the Prophet. His descendant Khufaynah ibn Qays ibn Salamah ibn Tarif was killed with al-Husayn ibn Ali on the day of al-Taff.

names.arabic: سلمة بن طريف بن أبان بن سلمة بن حارثة بن فهم الفهمي
خفينة بن قيس بن سلمة بن طريف
names.english: Khufaynah ibn Qays ibn Salamah ibn Tarif

records.arabic: في أحمر بن سليم
records.english: See Aḥmar ibn Sulaym.

records.arabic: بن غانم بن عامر بن عبد الله بن عويج بن كعب القرشي العدوي قال بن حبان له صحبة وقال أبو عمر رحل مع أمه إلى المدينة وكان من فضلاء المسلمين وصالحيهم واستعمله عمر على السوق وجمع الناس عليه في قيام رمضان قلت هذا كله كلام مصعب الزبيري وذكره عنه الزبير بن بكار وقد ذكره بن سعد فيمن رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يحفظ عنه وذكره أباه في مسلمة الفتح وقال في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي أهل المدينة ولد على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكره خليفة في الطبقة الأولى من أهل المدينة وقال بن منده سليمان بن أبي حثمة الأنصاري ذكر في الصحابة ولا يصح ثم ساق من طريق أبي بكر بن سليمان بن أبي حثمة عن أبيه قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكبر على جنائزنا أربعا وخمسا قلت قوله الأنصاري وهم وقد روى عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن الزهري عن سليمان بن أبي حثمة عن أمه الشفاء قالت دخل علي عمر وعندي رجلان نائمان تعني زوجها أبا حثمة وابنها سليمان فقال أما صليا الصبح قلت لم يزالا يصليان حتى أصبحنا فصليا الصبح وناما فقال لأن أشهد الصبح في جماعة أحب إلي من قيام ليلة وأخرجه بن جريج عن بن أبي مليكة قال جاءت الشفاء إلى عمر فقال مالي لا أرى أبا حثمة فقالت دأب ليلته فكسل أن يخرج فصلى الصبح ثم رقد فذكر نحوه وأخرجه مالك عن بن شهاب عن أبي بكر بن سليمان بن أبي حثمة أن عمر فقد سليمان بن أبي حثمة في صلاة الصبح فغدا على مسكنه فمر على الشفاء فسألها فذكره وقال الزبير بن بكار حدثني محمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن طلحة قال اصطلح الناس بأذرح يعني في زمان التحكيم على سليمان بن أبي حثمة يصلي بهم وكان قارئا مسنا
records.english: ibn Ghānim ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUwayj ibn Kaʿb, al-Qurashi al-Adawi. Ibn Hibban said that he had companionship. Abu Umar said that he traveled with his mother to Medina, was one of the virtuous and righteous Muslims, and was appointed by Umar over the market. Umar also gathered the people behind him for the Ramadan night prayer. I say: all of this is the wording of Mus'ab al-Zubayri, as related from him by al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar. Ibn Sa'd listed Sulayman among those who saw the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم but preserved nothing from him; he listed his father among those who accepted Islam at the Conquest. Among the first class of the Successors of Medina, Ibn Sa'd wrote that Sulayman was born during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Khalifah included him in the first class of the people of Medina. Ibn Mandah said: ‘Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah al-Ansari was listed among the Companions, but that is unsound.’ He then transmitted, by way of Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah, from his father: ‘The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم would pronounce four or five takbirs over our dead.’ I say: calling him Ansari is an error. Abd al-Razzaq transmitted, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah, from his mother al-Shifa, who said: ‘Umar entered upon me while two men were asleep in my house’—meaning her husband Abu Hathmah and her son Sulayman. He asked, ‘Did they not pray the dawn prayer?’ I replied, ‘They continued praying until morning, then prayed the dawn prayer and went to sleep.’ He said, ‘That I should attend the dawn prayer in congregation is dearer to me than spending a whole night in prayer.’ Ibn Jurayj also transmitted, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: ‘Al-Shifa came to Umar, and he asked, “Why do I not see Abu Hathmah?” She replied, “He exerted himself in worship through the night, so he lacked the energy to go out. He prayed the dawn prayer and then lay down.”’ He then related a similar report. Malik transmitted from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah, that Umar noticed Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah's absence from the dawn prayer. In the morning he went to his dwelling, passed al-Shifa, asked her about him, and related the report. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me, from Muhammad ibn Talhah, who said: ‘At Adhruh’—meaning at the time of the arbitration—‘the people agreed that Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah should lead them in prayer. He was an elderly reciter of the Qur'an.’

names.arabic: سليمان بن أبي حثمة بن غانم بن عامر بن عبد الله بن عويج بن كعب القرشي العدوي
أبي بكر بن سليمان بن أبي حثمة
names.english: Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي وكان يكنى به وكان أكبر ولده قال الزبير بن بكار أمة كبشة بنت هوذة بن أبي عمرو العذرية
records.english: ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī. He was given a kunyah on account of him, and he was the eldest of his children. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said that his mother was Kabshah bint Hawdhah ibn Abi Amr al-Udhriyyah.

records.arabic: بن عتبة بن أبي وقاص الزهري لأبيه صحبة وروى بن منده من طريق إسماعيل بن محمد بن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسليمان بن هاشم بن عتبة فوضعه في حجره فبال عليه فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقدح من ماء فصبه على مباله حيث بال ما زاد على ذلك وزعم بن الأثير أن اسم والد عتبة المذكور ربيعة بن عبد شمس وفيه نظر لأن البخاري ذكر في ترجمة محمد بن إسماعيل بن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال بن فضيل عن محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن إسماعيل بن أبي وقاص قال أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسليمان بن هاشم بن أبي وقاص فصب على مباله انتهى فهذا وإن كان فيه بعض مخالفة لكنه شاهد لأن القصة إنما وقعت لشخص من آل أبي وقاص لا من آل ربيعة بن عبد شمس وأيضا فإن أهل النسب لم يذكروا في آل عتبة بن ربيعة أحدا اسمه سليمان بن هاشم وذكروه في آل أبي وقاص فثبت ما قلته والله أعلم
records.english: ibn ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ al-Zuhrī. His father had companionship, and Ibn Mandah transmitted, by way of Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: ‘Sulayman ibn Hashim ibn Utbah was brought to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. He placed the child in his lap, and the child urinated upon him. A cup of water was brought to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he poured it over the spot where the child had urinated, doing nothing beyond that.’ Ibn al-Athir claimed that the father of the aforementioned Utbah was Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams. This is open to question, for al-Bukhari wrote in the notice of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: ‘Ibn Fudayl transmitted from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: Sulayman ibn Hashim ibn Abi Waqqas was brought to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he poured water over the child's urine.’ End quote. Although this contains some disagreement with the preceding form, it corroborates it, for the incident occurred to a person of the family of Abi Waqqas, not of the family of Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams. Furthermore, the genealogists mention no one named Sulayman ibn Hashim among the descendants of Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, but they do mention him among the descendants of Abi Waqqas. Thus what I have said is established. والله أعلم.

records.arabic: بن المحبق الهذلي لأبيه صحبة قال بن أبي حاتم في المراسيل سئل أبو زرعة عن سنان بن سلمة أن له صحبة فقال لا ولكن ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن بن الأعرابي أنه ولد يوم حنين فبشر به أبوه فقال لسنان اطعن به في سبيل الله أحب إلي منه فسماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سنانا وروى وكيع عن أبيه عن سنان بن سلمة قال ولدت يوم حرب كان للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسماني سنانا وقال العسكري ولد سنان بعد الفتح فسماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان شجاعا بطلا قلت وقد روى سنان عن أبيه وعن عمر وابن عباس وأرسل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحديثه عنه عند الطبراني ولفظه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث معه بهدي الحديث أخرجه من طريق الفريابي عن الثوري عن عبد الكريم بن أبي المخارق عن معاذ بن سعوة عنه وقد اختلف فيه على الثوري وعلى شيخه ورواه بن جريج عن عبد الكريم فقال عن معاذ عن سنان بن سلمة عن أبيه أخرجه أحمد عن محمد بن بكر عنه وقال أبو عاصم عن بن جريج فقال بسنده عن سنان بن سلمة عن سلمة بن المحبق أخرجه يعقوب بن سفيان عنه والدارقطني من طريق أخرى عن أبي عاصم وروى عنه قتادة وسلم بن جنادة وغيرهما ونزل البصرة قال خليفة ولاه زياد غزو الهند سنة خمسين وله خبر عجيب في ذلك وقال عمر بن شبة ولاه مصعب البصرة لما خرج لقتال عبد الملك بن مروان سنة اثنتين وسبعين وذكره بن سعد في التابعين في الطبقة الأولى من أهل البصرة قال العجلي تابعي ثقة وقال بن حبان في الصحابة مات في آخر ولاية الحجاج
records.english: ibn al-Muḥabbiq al-Hudhalī. His father had companionship. Ibn Abī Ḥātim said in al-Marasil: ‘Abu Zur'ah was asked whether Sinan ibn Salamah had companionship. He replied, “No, but he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.”’ Ibn al-A'rabi related that Sinan was born on the day of Hunayn. When his father was congratulated on his birth, he said, ‘A spear with which I might thrust in the path of God would be dearer to me than he.’ The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم therefore named him Sinan. Waki transmitted from his father, from Sinan ibn Salamah, who said: ‘I was born on the day of a battle fought by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and he named me Sinan.’ Al-Askari said: ‘Sinan was born after the Conquest. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم named him, and he was brave and heroic.’ I say: Sinan transmitted from his father, from Umar, and from Ibn Abbas, and he transmitted disconnected reports from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. His hadith from the Prophet appears in al-Tabarani with the wording that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent sacrificial animals with him—and related the hadith. Al-Tabarani transmitted it by way of al-Firyabi, from al-Thawri, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq, from Mu'adh ibn Sa'wah, from Sinan. The transmitters disagreed concerning it from al-Thawri and from al-Thawri's shaykh. Ibn Jurayj transmitted it from Abd al-Karim with the wording: from Mu'adh, from Sinan ibn Salamah, from his father. Ahmad transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Bakr, from Ibn Jurayj. Abu Asim transmitted from Ibn Jurayj and gave his chain as: from Sinan ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn al-Muhabbiq. Ya'qub ibn Sufyan transmitted it from Abu Asim, as did al-Daraqutni through another route from Abu Asim. Qatadah, Salm ibn Junadah, and others transmitted from Sinan. He settled in Basra. Khalifah said that Ziyad placed him in command of the expedition to India in the year fifty, and Sinan had an extraordinary story concerning it. Umar ibn Shabbah said that Mus'ab placed him in command of Basra when Mus'ab set out to fight Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan in the year seventy-two. Ibn Sa'd included him in the first class of the Successors of Basra. Al-Ijli said, ‘A trustworthy Successor.’ Ibn Hibban included him among the Companions and said that he died near the end of al-Hajjaj's governorship.

records.arabic:
شاعر مخضرم ذكره المرزباني وأنشد له وقال أبو القاسم الحسن بن بشر الآمدي ساعدة بن جؤية أحد بني كعب بن كاهل بن الحارث بن سعد الهذلي شاعر محسن جاهلي وشعره محشو بالغريب والمعاني الغامضة وهو القائل في صفة سيف
ترى أثره في صفحتيه كأنه
مدارج شبثان لهن دبيب قال وهو جمع شبث بمعجمه وموحدة مفتوحة ثم مثلثة دويبة كثيرة الأرجل
records.english: a poet who lived across the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. Al-Marzubānī mentioned him and cited verses of his. Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Amidi said: ‘Sa'idah ibn Ju'ayyah, of the Banu Ka'b ibn Kahil ibn al-Harith ibn Sa'd al-Hudhali, was an accomplished pre-Islamic poet. His poetry is filled with rare vocabulary and subtle meanings. Describing a sword, he said: “You see the marks upon its two faces as though / they were paths traced by creeping shabathan.”’ Al-Amidi said: ‘Shabathan, with a dotted shin, an open ba, and then a tha, is the plural of shabath, a small creature with many legs.’

records.arabic: مولى قدامة بن مظعون له إدراك قال أبو عمر في التمهيد قال عبد الملك بن الماجشون بلغنا أن عمر قال لمولى لقدامة بن مظعون يقال له سالم إذا رأيت من يقطع من السمر شيئا يعني بالمدينة فخذ فأسه قال وثوبه يا أمير المؤمنين قال لا
records.english: the client of Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Abū ʿUmar said in al-Tamhīd: ʿAbd … said—that is, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mājishūn—‘It has reached us that ʿUmar said to a client of Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn called Sālim: “If you see anyone cutting anything from the samur trees”—meaning in Medina—“take his axe.” He said, “And his garment, Commander of the Believers?” He replied, “No.”’

records.arabic:
بن دارة الشاعر المشهور قال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني أدرك الجاهلية والإسلام ودارة لقلب غلب على جده واسمه يربوع بن كعب بن عدي بن جشم بن بهثة بن عبد الله بن غطفان ذكره أبو عبيدة قال وأخوه عبد الرحمن بن دارة من شعراء الإسلام وقال المرزباني هو سالم بن مسافع بن عقبة بن شريح بن يربوع وساق نسبه قال وقيل أن دارة أم سالم نفسه وقيل اسم جدته وقيل لقب شريح جد مسافع وقرأت في ديوان شعر سالم أنه قتل في خلافة عثمان قتله زميل بن أم دينار الفزاري لأن سالما كان هجاه بقوله المشهور
لا تأمنن فزاريا خلوت به
على قلوصك وأكتبها بأسيار وبقول فيها
أنا بن دارة موصولا به نسبي
وهل بدارة يا للناس من عار قلت وهو يشعر بأن دارة لقب جده كما قال أبو عبيدة ولما قيل فيه
فلا تكثروا فيها الضجاج فإنه
محا السيف ما قال بن دارة اجمعا وقال دعبل بن علي في طبقات الشعراء وأنشد له يخاطب عيينة بن حصن الفزاري وكان قد ارتد في خلافة أبي بكر ثم عاد إلى الإسلام وقال لأبي بكر قصتي وقصة الأشعث واحدة فما بالكم اكرمتموه وزوجتموه ولم تفعلوا ذلك بي وكان أبو بكر زوج الأشعث أخته فأجاب سالم بن دارة عيينة عن ذلك بقوله
يا عيينة بن حصن آل عدي
أنت من قومك الصميم صميم
لست كالأشعث المعصب بالتاج
غلاما قد ساد وهو فطيم
جده آكل المرار وقيس
خطبه في الملوك خطب عظيم
إن تكونا أتيتما خطتا الغدر
سواءكما يقد الأديم
فله هيبة الملوك وللأشعث
إن حان حادث وقديم
إن للأشعث بن قيس بن معدي
كرب عزة وأنت بهيم
records.english:
ibn Dārah, the famous poet. Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī said that he lived into Islam after the pre-Islamic period. The wording here is defective; it apparently means that Dārah was a sobriquet applied to his grandfather, whose name was Yarbūʿ ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAdī ibn Jusham ibn Bahthah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghaṭafān. Abū ʿUbaydah mentioned him and said that his brother ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Dārah was among the poets of Islam. Al-Marzubānī said: He was Sālim ibn Musāfiʿ ibn ʿUqbah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Yarbūʿ, and he gave his lineage. He said that Dārah was also said to have been Sālim's own mother, his grandmother's name, or the sobriquet of Shurayḥ, Musāfiʿ's grandfather. I read in Sālim's poetry collection that he was killed during ʿUthmān's caliphate. Zumayl ibn Umm Dīnār al-Fazārī killed him because Sālim had lampooned him in his famous lines:

Do not trust a Fazārī when you are alone with him
upon your young she-camel—and inscribe this upon the thongs.

And in a poem containing these lines:

I am the son of Dārah, my lineage joined to him;
is Dārah, O people, any cause for shame?

I say: This suggests that Dārah was his grandfather's sobriquet, as Abū ʿUbaydah said. When it was said concerning him:

Do not raise so much clamor over it, for
the sword erased all that Ibn Dārah said.

Diʿbil ibn ʿAlī said in Ṭabaqāt al-Shuʿarāʾ, and recited verses of his addressing ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī. ʿUyaynah had apostatized during Abū Bakr's caliphate and then returned to Islam. He said to Abū Bakr: ‘My case and al-Ashʿath's are the same. Why, then, did you honor him and marry him into your family but did not do that for me?’ Abū Bakr had married his sister to al-Ashʿath. Sālim ibn Dārah answered ʿUyaynah about that with these lines:

O ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn of the house of ʿAdī,
you are the very core of your people.
You are not like al-Ashʿath, crowned with a turban,
a youth who became a chief while still weaned.
His forefather is Ākil al-Murār, and Qays—
his standing among kings is a mighty standing.
Though you both committed the two acts of treachery,
likening the two of you would cut the very hide.
He possesses the awe of kings, and al-Ashʿath has
an ancient standing whenever an event comes.
Indeed al-Ashʿath ibn Qays ibn Maʿdī
Karib possesses might, while you are a brute.

records.arabic: آخره نون أو راء له إدراك روى بن وهب عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن عن السائب بن مهجان رجل من أهل إيلياء وكان قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لما دخل عمر حمد الله وأثنى عليه ثم قال أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قام فينا خطيبا كمقامي فيكم فأمر بتقوى الله الحديث أخرجه بن عساكر من طريق جعفر بن أحمد بن سنان عن عباس الدوري عن هارون بن معروف عن بن وهب ومن طريق أخرى عن بن عباس لكن قال فيه وقد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكذا أخرجه البخاري عن يحيى بن سليمان عن بن وهب وذكره أبو زرعة الدمشقي في الطبقة العليا من تابعي أهل الشام وكذا صنع بن سميع وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين وقال أدرك عمر
records.english: Its final letter is nūn or rāʾ. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Ibn Wahb transmitted from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Sāʾib ibn Mihjān, a man of Aelia who had met the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He said: ‘When ʿUmar entered, he praised and extolled God, then said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم stood among us to deliver an address just as I stand among you, and he commanded the fear of God...”’ and he related the tradition. Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted it by way of Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbbās al-Dūrī, from Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf, from Ibn Wahb. He also transmitted it by another route from Ibn ʿAbbās, though that version says that he had met the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Al-Bukhārī likewise transmitted it from Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān, from Ibn Wahb. Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī placed him in the senior generation of the Successors of Syria, as did Ibn Sumayʿ. Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the trustworthy Successors and said that he met ʿUmar.

records.arabic: الحنفي اليمامي له إدراك قال وثيمة في الردة أنه سبي يوم اليمامة وهو شيخ كبير وذكر عنه كلاما كثيرا يخبر فيه أنه ثبت على إسلامه ونهى مسيلمة وقومه عن الردة فعذره خالد بذلك والله أعلم
records.english: al-Ḥanafī al-Yamāmī. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Wathīmah said in al-Riddah that he was taken captive on the day of al-Yamāmah when he was a very old man. He related at length from him that he had remained steadfast in his Islam and had forbidden Musaylimah and his people from apostasy. Khālid therefore excused him. والله أعلم

records.arabic: بكسر أوله وسكون الجيم وآخره فاء شيخ أدرك الجاهلية وسمع من معاذ بن جبل ذكره البخاري في تاريخه
records.english: with kasrah on its first letter, sukūn on the jīm, and fāʾ as its final letter; an elder who lived in the pre-Islamic period and heard from Muʿādh ibn Jabal. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him in his Tārīkh.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الذي يضرب به المثل في البلاغة ذكره بن عساكر في تاريخه وقال بلغني وفد على معاوية قلت أن ثبت هذا فهو من أهل هذا القسم فإن المعروف أنه جاهلي وقال أبو نعيم في كتاب طبقات الخطباء كان سحبان خطيب العرب غير مدافع وكان إذا خطب لم يعد حرفا ولم يتلعثم ولم يتوقف ولم يتفكر بل كان يسيل سيلا
records.english: the man proverbial for eloquence. Ibn ʿAsākir mentioned him in his History. He said: ‘I have been informed that he came in a delegation to Muʿāwiyah.’ I say: If this is established, he belongs among the people of this section, for what is well known is that he was a man of the pre-Islamic period. Abū Nuʿaym said in Ṭabaqāt al-Khuṭabāʾ: ‘Saḥbān was indisputably the orator of the Arabs. When he delivered an address, he did not repeat a letter, stammer, pause, or stop to think; rather, he poured forth like a torrent.’

records.arabic:
بمهملة مصغرا عبد لبني الحسحاس بمهملات شاعر مخضرم مشهور روى أبو الفرج الأصبهاني من طريق أبي عبيدة قال كان سحيم عبدا أسود أعجميا أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد تمثل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بشيء من شعره روى المرزباني في ترجمته والدينوري في المجالسة من طريق علي بن زيد عن الحسن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال
كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا
فقال أبو بكر إنما قال الشاعر كفى الشيب والإسلام للمرء ناهيا فأعادها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كالأول فقال أبو بكر أشهد إنك لرسول الله وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له وقال عمر بن شبة قدم سحيم بعد ذلك على عمر فأنشده القصيدة أنبأنا بذلك معاذ بن جبل عن بن عوف عن بن سيرين قال فقال له لو قدمت الإسلام على الشيب لأجزتك وأخرج البخاري في الأدب المفرد من طريق سعيد بن عبد الرحمن عن السائب عن عمر أنه كان لا يمر على أحد يعد أن يفيء الفيء الا أقامه ثم بينا هو كذلك إذ أقبل مولى بني الحسحاس يقول الشعر فدعا به فقال كيف قلت قال
ودع سليمي أن تجهزت غاديا
كفى الشيب والأسلام للمرء ناهيا فقال حسبك صدقت صدقت وقد قيل أن سحيما قتل في خلافة عثمان ويقال أن سبب قتله أن امرأة من بني الحسحاس اسرها بعض اليهود فاستخصها لنفسه وجعلها في حصن له فبلغ ذلك سحيما فأخذته الغيرة فما زال يتحيل حتى تسور على اليهودي حصنه فقتله وخلص المرأة فأوصلها إلى قومه فلقيته يوما فقالت له يا سحيم والله لوددت إني قدرت على مكافأتك على تخليصي من اليهودي فقال لها والله انك لقادرة على ذلك وعرض لها بنفسها فاستحيت وذهبت ثم لقيته مرة أخرى فعرض لها بذلك فأطاعته وهويها وطفق يتغزل فيها وكان اسمها سمية ففطنوا له فقتلوه خشية العار عليهم بسبب سمية وقال بن حبيب أنشدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قول سحيم عبد بني الحسحاس
الحمد لله حمدا لا انقطاع له
فليس إحسانه عنا بمقطوع فقال أحسن وصدق وإن الله ليشكر مثل هذا وان سدد وقارب أنه لمن أهل الجنة
records.english:
with an undotted initial letter, in the diminutive; a slave of the Banū al-Ḥasḥās—spelled with undotted letters—and a famous poet who lived across the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. He transmitted—Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī did—by way of Abū ʿUbaydah: Suḥaym was a Black, non-Arab slave who lived into the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم quoted some of his poetry. Al-Marzubānī, in his entry, and al-Dīnawarī, in al-Majālasah, related by way of ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan, that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said:

Islam and gray hair suffice to restrain a man.

Abū Bakr said, ‘The poet actually said: “Gray hair and Islam suffice to restrain a man.”’ The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم repeated it as he had the first time, so Abū Bakr said, ‘I testify that you are the Messenger of God: “We did not teach him poetry, nor does it befit him.”’ ʿUmar ibn Shabbah said that Suḥaym later came to ʿUmar and recited the poem to him. We were informed of this by Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Ibn Sīrīn, who said that ʿUmar told him, ‘Had you put Islam before gray hair, I would have rewarded you.’ Al-Bukhārī transmitted in al-Adab al-Mufrad, by way of Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Sāʾib, from ʿUmar, that whenever he passed anyone after the shade had begun to turn, he would make him rise. While he was doing so, the client of the Banū al-Ḥasḥās approached reciting poetry. He summoned him and asked, ‘How did you say it?’ He replied:

Bid farewell to Sulaymā when you prepare to leave at dawn;
gray hair and Islam suffice to restrain a man.

He said, ‘Enough. You have spoken truth, you have spoken truth.’ It is also said that Suḥaym was killed during ʿUthmān's caliphate. The reported cause was that some Jews had captured a woman of the Banū al-Ḥasḥās. One of them took her for himself and placed her in a fortress. When this reached Suḥaym, his sense of honor was aroused, and he kept devising a way until he scaled the Jew's fortress, killed him, freed the woman, and returned her to her people. One day she met him and said, ‘Suḥaym, by God, I wish I were able to repay you for freeing me from the Jew.’ He said, ‘By God, you are able to do that,’ and propositioned her. She felt ashamed and left. When he met her another time, he propositioned her again, and she yielded to him. He fell in love with her and began composing love poetry about her. Her name was Sumayyah. They discovered what had happened and killed him, fearing the disgrace that Sumayyah would bring upon them. Ibn Ḥabīb said: The words of Suḥaym, slave of the Banū al-Ḥasḥās, were recited to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم:

Praise belongs to God, a praise that never ceases,
for His beneficence toward us is never cut off.

He said, ‘He expressed it well and spoke truly. God surely rewards the like of this; if he acted rightly and kept close to the mark, he would indeed be among the people of Paradise.’

records.arabic:
بالمثلثه مصغرا الرياحي بالتحتانية شاعر مخضرم قال بن دريد عاش في الجاهلية أربعين وفي الإسلام ستين وله أخبار مع زياد بن أبيه وقد تقدمت له قصة مع سمرة بن عمرو العنبري وذكر المرزباني أنه هو الذي تفاخر هو وغالب بن صعصعة والد الفرزدق فتناحرا الإبل فبلغ عليا فقال لا تأكلوا منه شيئا فإنه أهل به لغير الله وأخرجها سعيد بن منصور سمعت ربعي بن عبد الله بن الجارود سمعت الجارود بن أبي سبرة فذكر القصة في المنافرة والمناحرة وحاصل القصة فيما ذكر أهل الأخبار أن غالبا وسحيما خرجا في رفقة وقد حزبت بلادهم وفي خلافة عثمان فنحر غالب ناقة وأطعم فنحر سحيم ناقة فقيل لغالب إنه يؤائمك فقال بل هو كريم ثم نحر غالب ناقتين فنحر سحيم ناقتين ثم نحر غالب عشرا فنحر سحيم عشرا فقال غالب الآن علمت أنه يؤاثمني فسكت إلى أن وردت إبله وكانت مائتي وقيل أربعمائة فعقرها كلها فلم يعقر سحيم شيئا ثم استدرك ذلك في خلافة علي فعقر بالكناسة مثلها فقال علي لا تأكلوها قال المرزباني وسحيم هو القائل
أنا بن جلا وطلاع الثنايا
متى أضع العمامة تعرفوني
وماذا يدرك الشعراء مني
وقد جاوزت حد الأربعين
أخو خمسين مجتمع اشدي
وتجديني مداورة الشؤون
records.english:
with a thāʾ, in the diminutive; al-Riyāḥī, with a yāʾ, a poet who lived across the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. Ibn … said—namely, Ibn Durayd—that he lived forty years in the pre-Islamic period and sixty in Islam. He had accounts involving Ziyād ibn Abīh, and a story involving Samurah ibn ʿAmr al-ʿAnbarī has already appeared. Al-Marzubānī mentioned that he and Ghālib ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah, the father of al-Farazdaq, were the two men who competed in boasting and slaughtered camels against one another. News of it reached ʿAlī, who said, ‘Do not eat any of them, for they were dedicated to other than God.’ Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr also transmitted the report: ‘I heard Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jārūd say: I heard al-Jārūd ibn Abī Sabrah...’ and he related the story of their contest in boasting and slaughter. The substance of the account as the transmitters of reports tell it is that Ghālib and Suḥaym set out in a company at a time when drought had afflicted their lands, during ʿUthmān's caliphate. Ghālib slaughtered one she-camel and fed the people, so Suḥaym slaughtered one. Ghālib was told, ‘He is matching you.’ He replied, ‘No, he is simply generous.’ Then Ghālib slaughtered two she-camels, and Suḥaym slaughtered two; Ghālib slaughtered ten, and Suḥaym slaughtered ten. Ghālib then said, ‘Now I know that he is trying to rival me in sin.’ He remained silent until his camels arrived—two hundred, though it is also said four hundred—and hamstrung every one of them. Suḥaym slaughtered nothing. He later made up for it during ʿAlī's caliphate by hamstringing the same number at al-Kunāsah, whereupon ʿAlī said, ‘Do not eat them.’ Al-Marzubānī said that Suḥaym was the one who said:

I am the son of Jalā, the climber of mountain passes;
when I put on the turban, you will recognize me.
What can the poets attain against me,
when I have passed the age of forty?
A brother of fifty, with my full strength gathered,
yet the turning of affairs still tests me.

names.arabic: ربعي بن عبد الله بن الجارود
names.english: Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jārūd

records.arabic: مولى عتبة بن فرقد له إدراك وقد اوفده مولاه على عمر روى ذلك الحارث بن أبي أسامة من طريق أبي عثمان النهدي قال وكنت مع عتبة بن فرقد بأذربيجان فبعث مولاه سحيما وآخر على ثلاث رواحل إلى عمر فقدم على عمر فذكر قصته وإسناده صحيح
records.english: the client of ʿUtbah ibn Farqad. He lived to the beginning of Islam, and his patron sent him as an envoy to ʿUmar. This was transmitted by al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah by way of Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, who said: ‘I was with ʿUtbah ibn Farqad in Azerbaijan. He sent his client Suḥaym and another man to ʿUmar with three riding animals. He came to ʿUmar,’ and he related his story. Its chain of transmission is sound.

records.arabic: العدوي له إدراك قال أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة حدثنا مرحوم بن عبد العزيز عن أبيه عن سديس العدوي قال غزونا الأبلة فظفرنا بهم ثم انتهينا إلى الأهواز فظفرنا بهم وسبينا كثيرا فوقعنا على النساء فكتب أميرنا إلى عمر فذكر قصته ولعله شويس الآتي في المعجمة فليحرر
records.english: al-ʿAdawī. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah said: Marḥūm ibn ʿAbd … narrated to us—the full name is Marḥūm ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz—from his father, from Sudays al-ʿAdawī, who said: ‘We campaigned against al-Ubullah and defeated its people. Then we reached al-Ahwāz and defeated them, taking many captives. We had intercourse with the women, so our commander wrote to ʿUmar,’ and he related his story. He may be Shuways, who will appear under the pointed letter; this should be critically verified.

records.arabic: والد عبد الأعلى قال بن عساكر أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد اليرموك ثم روى من طريق عبد الأعلى بن سراقة عن أبيه قال انتهينا إلى أبي هريرة يوم اليرموك وهو يقول تزينوا للحور العين
records.english: the father of ʿAbd al-Aʿlā. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he lived during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He witnessed al-Yarmūk. He then related by way of ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Surāqah, from his father, who said: ‘We came to Abū Hurayrah on the day of al-Yarmūk while he was saying, “Adorn yourselves for the houris of Paradise.”’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بكسر الراء بعدها الجيم اليرموكي من أهل الكتاب أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأسلم بعده وروى الدولابي في الكنى من طريق حماد بن سلمة عن يعلى بن عطاء عن بجير أبي عبيد عن سرج اليرموكي قال أجد في الكتاب أن هذه الآية اثني عشر رئيسا نبيهم أحدهم فإذا وفت العدة طغوا وبغوا وكان بأسهم بينهم قال وكان عبد الله بن عمر يتعلم من سرج هذا
records.english: with kasrah on the rāʾ, followed by jīm; al-Yarmūkī, one of the People of the Book. He lived during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and embraced Islam after his death. Al-Dūlābī related in al-Kunā, by way of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Bujayr Abū ʿUbayd, from Sirj al-Yarmūkī, who said: ‘I find in the Book that this sign consists of twelve chiefs, their prophet being one of them. When the prescribed number is complete, they will grow tyrannical and transgress, and their might will be turned against one another.’ He said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar used to learn from this Sirj.

records.arabic: بن أبي إياس أبو عمرو الشيباني أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقدم بعده ثم نزل الكوفة واتفقوا على توثيقه وروى الطبراني من طريق عيسى بن عبد الرحمن سمعت أبا عمرو الشيباني يقول بلغنا خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا أرعى إبلا على أهلي بكاظمة ويقال أدرك من حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين سنة والأصح دون ذلك وروى عن أبي مسعود وعلي وحذيفة وغيرهم روى عنه أبو إسحاق الشيباني والحارث بن شبل والوليد بن العيزار والأعمش وآخرون قال إسماعيل بن أبي خالد عاش مائة وعشرين سنة قلت فكأنه مات سنة ست وتسعين وقد أرخه بن عبد البر سنة خمس وهو قريب وزعم بن حبان أن القادسية كانت سنة إحدى وعشرين فيكون مات سنة إحدى ومائة وسماه بن حبان سعيدا وقال أبو نعيم سعد أو سعيد والأصح سعد وهو مشهور بكنيته
records.english: ibn Abī Iyās, Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī. He lived during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and came after his death, then settled in Kufa. Scholars agreed that he was trustworthy. Al-Ṭabarānī related by way of ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: ‘I heard Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī say, “News reached us of the emergence of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while I was pasturing camels for my family at Kāẓimah.”’ It is said that he lived for forty years during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, though the sounder view is that it was less than that. He related from Abū Masʿūd, ʿAlī, Ḥudhayfah, and others. Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, al-Ḥārith ibn Shibl, al-Walīd ibn al-ʿAyzār, al-Aʿmash, and others related from him. Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid said that he lived for 120 years. I say: It would therefore seem that he died in the year 96. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr dated his death to 95, which is close. Ibn Ḥibbān claimed that al-Qādisiyyah occurred in the year 21, in which case he would have died in 101. Ibn Ḥibbān called him Saʿīd. Abū Nuʿaym said: ‘Saʿd, or Saʿīd’; the sounder form is Saʿd, and he is famous by his kunya.

names.arabic: سعد بن إياس بن أبي إياس أبو عمرو الشيباني
names.english: Saʿd ibn Iyās ibn Abī Iyās, Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الفارسي كان ممن أعان على قتل الأسود العنسي ذكره الواقدي في الردة عن إسماعيل بن أبي ربيعة عن أبيه قال ولما قتل الأسود وقف سعد المذكور في نفر من المسلمين فمن مر من أصحاب الأسود فشهد أن الأسود كذاب وإلا قتلوه
records.english: al-Fārisī. He was among those who helped kill al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī. He was mentioned by al-Wāqidī in al-Riddah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Rabīʿah, from his father. He said: When al-Aswad was killed, the aforementioned Saʿd stood with a group of Muslims. Anyone among al-Aswad's followers who passed by had either to testify that al-Aswad was a liar or be killed.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له صحبة روى أحمد بن حنبل قوله في كتاب الإيمان قلت الذي في كتاب الإيمان لأحمد من طريق بن إسحاق حدثني عبد الله بن أبي بكر ويحيى بن سعد إنهما حدثاه عن سعيد بن عمارة أخي بني سعد بن بكر وكانت له صحبة فذكر الأثر المتقدم في ترجمة سعد بن عمارة أخي سعد بن عمارة وقد تقدم أنه قيل فيه سعد وسعيد وكأن النسخة التي وقعت للذهني تصفحت قوله أخي بني فصارت أخبرني فخرج من ذلك أن سعد بن بكر له صحبة والواقع أن قوله وكانت له صحبة المراد بذلك سعد بن عمارة وأما سعد بن بكر فهو جده الأعلى وهو بطن كبير في ذرية جماعة من الصحابة بينهم مبينه عدة آباء والله المستعان
records.english: He had companionship. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal transmitted his statement in Kitāb al-Īmān. I say: the one who appears in Aḥmad's Kitāb al-Īmān is identified in a report transmitted by way of Ibn Isḥāq: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿd related to me that they had been told by Saʿīd ibn ʿUmārah, a brother of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr, who had companionship,’ and he mentioned the report that already appeared in the entry on Saʿd ibn ʿUmārah, a brother of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr. It has already been stated that his name was variously given as Saʿd and Saʿīd. It seems that in the copy that reached al-Dhuhnī, the words ‘a brother of the Banū’ were corrupted into ‘he informed me,’ producing the claim that Saʿd ibn Bakr had companionship. In reality, the words ‘who had companionship’ refer to Saʿd ibn ʿUmārah. As for Saʿd ibn Bakr, he is his remote ancestor and the eponym of a large tribal subdivision. Among his descendants were several Companions, separated from him by a number of generations. والله المستعان

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الفزاري له إدراك وذكر سيف في الفتوح أن سعد بن أبي وقاص اوفده على عمر بفتح القادسية
records.english: al-Fazārī. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ sent him to ʿUmar with news of the conquest of al-Qādisiyyah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأعرج ويقال الأقرع اليماني أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ووفد على عمر روى البخاري في تاريخه من طريق سماك بن الفضل عن شهاب بن عبد الله عن سعد الأعرج أنه قدم المدينة فقال له عمر أين تريد قال الجهاد قال ارجع إلى صاحبك يعني يعلى بن أمية ويعلى يومئذ على اليمن فإن عملا بحق جهاد حسن وأخرجه عبد الرزاق مطولا وأخرج محمد بن الحسن في الآثار عن أبي حنيفة عن عطاء بن السائب عن الحسن أن عمر بعث سعد بن مالك أو سعيدا مصدقا
records.english: al-Aʿraj, also said to be al-Aqraʿ, al-Yamānī. He lived during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and came in a delegation to ʿUmar. Al-Bukhārī related in his Tārīkh, by way of Sammāk ibn al-Faḍl, from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Saʿd al-Aʿraj, that he came to Medina. ʿUmar asked him, ‘Where are you bound?’ He replied, ‘For jihad.’ ʿUmar said, ‘Return to your superior’—meaning Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, who was then governor of Yemen—‘for properly discharging an office is excellent jihad.’ ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it at greater length. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan transmitted in al-Āthār, from Abū Ḥanīfah, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from al-Ḥasan, that ʿUmar sent Saʿd ibn Mālik—or Saʿīd—as a collector of alms.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك وكان عاملا لعمر على الجار روى عنه ابنه عبد الله وذكر ذلك بن حبان في ثقات التابعين وقد تقدم في القسم الأول سعيد بن نوفل وأنه مختلف في صحبته فيحتمل أن يكون هذا هو ذاك
records.english: He lived to the beginning of Islam and was ʿUmar’s governor over al-Jār. His son ʿAbd … transmitted from him; his son's full name was ʿAbd Allāh. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned this in his collection of trustworthy Successors. There has already appeared in the first section a Saʿīd ibn Nawfal, about whose companionship there is disagreement; this man may be the same person.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الواقدي فيمن أسلم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل سبأ
records.english: Al-Wāqidī listed him among those who accepted Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He was one of the people of Sabaʾ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: مولى الأسود بن سفيان له إدراك وسماع من عمر روى عنه ابنه عبد الرحمن وذكره البخاري في تاريخه وابن أبي حاتم
records.english: the client of al-Aswad ibn Sufyān. He lived to the beginning of Islam and heard from ʿUmar. His son ʿAbd … transmitted from him; his son's full name was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him in his Tārīkh, as did Ibn Abī Ḥātim.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الهذلي مخضرم ذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء ولم يذكر له شعرا
records.english: al-Hudhalī, one who lived across the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. Al-Marzubānī mentioned him in Muʿjam al-Shuʿarāʾ but did not mention any poetry of his.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: آخره راء بن مالك العبسي أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسمع من عمر روى عنه حلام بن صالح ذكره البخاري وابن حبان في التابعين وقد تقدم في الأول سعر بن سوادة وأن العسكري ذكره في المخضرمين وهو غير هذا
records.english: ending in rāʾ; ibn Mālik al-ʿAbsī. He lived during the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and heard from ʿUmar. Ḥallām ibn Ṣāliḥ related from him. Al-Bukhārī and Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the Successors. Siʿr ibn Sawādah appeared earlier in the first section, where it was noted that al-ʿAskarī listed him among the mukhaḍrams; he is not this man.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: تقدم في الأول ونبهت على أنه من أهل هذا القسم
records.english: He appeared earlier in the first section, where I noted that he belongs in this section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مرة بن عمران بن رباح بن سالم بن غاضرة بن حبشية بن كعب الخزاعي له إدراك وكان على شرطة علي وولاه أذربيجان ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: ibn Murrah ibn ʿImrān ibn Rabāḥ ibn Sālim ibn Ghāḍirah ibn Ḥabashiyyah ibn Kaʿb al-Khuzāʿī lived into Islam. He commanded ʿAlī's guard, and ʿAlī appointed him governor of Azerbaijan. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him.

names.arabic: سعيد بن سارية بن مرة بن عمران بن رباح بن سالم بن غاضرة بن حبشية بن كعب الخزاعي
names.english: Saʿīd ibn Sāriyah ibn Murrah ibn ʿImrān ibn Rabāḥ ibn Sālim ibn Ghāḍirah ibn Ḥabashiyyah ibn Kaʿb al-Khuzāʿī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: وورد أحد الخمسة الذين كتب إليهم أبو بكر الصديق بمعاونة فيروز على الأسود العنسي ومظاهرته ذكره سيف وغيره
records.english: He is reported as one of the five to whom Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq wrote. He instructed them to assist Fayrūz against al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī and support him. Sayf and others mentioned him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العدوي ذكر سيف والطبراني أن خالد بن الوليد أوفده على أبي بكر الصديق بما فضل من الخمس بعد النفل ومبشرا بالفتح
records.english: al-ʿAdawī. Sayf and al-Ṭabarānī mentioned that Khālid ibn al-Walīd sent him as an envoy to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq with what remained of the fifth after the discretionary awards, and as the bearer of good news of the victory.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الهمداني له إدراك وقد شهد اليرموك وسمع من أبي بكر وعمر وكتب عن علي قاله خليفة وقال حمزة بن يوسف في تاريخ جرجان كان فيمن حمل مع حجر بن عدي يشفع فيه فترك فحول إلى جرجان فسكنها واختط بها وذكر سيف أن هاشم بن عتبة لما قدم بعد اليرموك فجعل في سبعين فيهم سعيد بن نمران وقال بن أبي خيثمة عن سليمان بن أبي شيخ أراد مصعب أن يوليه القضاء فمنه أخوه وكتب إليه إنه من أصحاب علي وروى مسدد في مسنده وابن المبارك في الزهد من طريق عامر البجلي عن سعيد بن نمران عن أبي بكر الصديق في قوله تعالى ثم استقاموا قال هم الذين لم يشركوا بالله شيئا وقال معاوية بن صالح عن يحيى بن معين في تسمية أهل الكوفة سعيد بن نمران سمع أبا بكر فقال مات في حدود السبعين
records.english: al-Hamdānī. He lived to the beginning of Islam, witnessed al-Yarmūk, and heard from Abū Bakr. He also heard from ʿUmar and served as a scribe for ʿAlī, according to Khalīfah. Ḥamzah ibn Yūsuf said in Tārīkh Jurjān: He was among those taken away with Ḥujr ibn ʿAdī; intercession was made on his behalf, and he was released, transferred to Jurjān, settled there, and marked out a residence for himself. Sayf mentioned that when Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah arrived after al-Yarmūk, he placed him among a group of seventy that included Saʿīd ibn Nimrān. Ibn Abī Khaythamah related from Sulaymān ibn Abī Shaykh that Muṣʿab wanted to appoint him to the judgeship, but his brother—so the defective wording apparently means—prevented him and wrote to Muṣʿab that he was one of ʿAlī's associates. Musaddad related in his Musnad, and Ibn al-Mubārak in al-Zuhd, by way of ʿĀmir al-Bajalī, from Saʿīd ibn Nimrān, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, concerning the Most High's words, ‘then remained steadfast’: ‘They are those who did not associate anything with God.’ Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, in his naming of the people of Kufa: ‘Saʿīd ibn Nimrān heard Abū Bakr.’ He died around the year 70.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الخيواني بالخاء المعجمة وسكون التحتانية له إدراك وسمع من معاذ بن جبل باليمن في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واستدركه بن فتحون وروى عن علي وابن مسعود وسلمان وحذيفة وغيرهم روى عنه ابنه عبد الرحمن وأبو إسحاق وعمارة بن عمير قال بن حبان هو الذي يقال له سعيد بن أبي حرة وقال بن سعيد لزم عليا حتى لقب القراد مات سنة خمس أو ست وتسعين وذكره في التابعين البخاري وابن سعد والعجلي
records.english: al-Khaywānī—with a dotted khāʾ and sukūn on the yāʾ. He lived to the beginning of Islam and heard from Muʿādh ibn Jabal in Yemen during the lifetime of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Ibn Fatḥūn supplied his entry. He related from ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Salmān, Ḥudhayfah, and others. His son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Isḥāq, and ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr related from him. Ibn Ḥibbān said: ‘He is the man called Saʿīd ibn Abī Ḥurrah.’ Ibn Saʿd said that he remained constantly with ʿAlī until he was nicknamed al-Qurrād. He died in the year 95 or 96. Al-Bukhārī, Ibn Saʿd, and al-ʿIjlī listed him among the Successors.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بسكون المهملة بعدها تحتانية بن غريض بفتح المعجمة وآخره معجمة بن عاديا التيماوي نسبة إلى تيماء التي بين الحجاز والشام وهو بن أخي السموءل بن عادياء اليهودي الذي يضرب به المثل في الوفاء أدرك الجاهلية والإسلام قال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني عمر طويلا وأدرك الإسلام فأسلم ومات في آخر خلافة معاوية ثم أسند عن الهيثم بن عدي قال حج معاوية فرأى شيخا يصلي في المسجد فقال من هذا قالوا سعية بن غريض فأرسل إليه فأتاه فذكر قصة طويلة في آخرها فقال معاوية قد خرف الشيخ فأقيموه وقد اختلف في الحرف الذي بعد العين في اسمه فقيل بالنون وقيل بالتحتانية وهو الراجح وتقدمت الإشارة إلى ذلك في القسم الأول
records.english: with sukūn on the undotted initial letter, followed by yāʾ; ibn Gharīḍ, with fatḥah on the dotted initial letter and a dotted final letter. His lineage continues through ibn ʿĀdiyā al-Taymāwī, an ascription to Taymāʾ, which lies between the Hijaz and Syria. He was the nephew of al-Samawʾal ibn ʿĀdiyāʾ, the Jew whose loyalty became proverbial. He lived through the pre-Islamic period and into Islam. Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī said that he lived a long life, reached Islam, embraced it, and died near the end of Muʿāwiyah's caliphate. He then transmitted from al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī, who said: Muʿāwiyah performed the pilgrimage and saw an old man praying in the mosque. He asked, ‘Who is this?’ They replied, ‘Saʿyah ibn Gharīḍ.’ He sent for him, and the man came. He related a long story at the end of which Muʿāwiyah said, ‘The old man has become senile; help him to his feet.’ There is disagreement over the letter after ʿayn in his name. It is said to be nūn and also yāʾ; the latter is stronger. This was noted earlier in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجذامي تقدم مع أخويه حصن وحصين وأنه كان ممن ثبت على إسلامه في الردة
records.english: al-Judhāmī. He appeared earlier with his two brothers, Ḥiṣn and Ḥuṣayn, with the statement that he was among those who remained steadfast in Islam during the apostasy.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: السلمي ذكر وثيمة أنه كان أحد من ثبت على إسلامه وعذل قومه على الردة وخطبهم خطبة بليغة فشتموه وأنشد له في ذلك شعرا قال فلما رأى إنهم لا يطيعونه رحل عنهم إلى المدينة فأقام بها
records.english: al-Sulamī. Wathīmah mentioned that he was one of those who remained steadfast in his Islam and reproached his people for their apostasy and delivered an eloquent address to them, but they insulted him. Wathīmah quoted poetry he composed about this. When Sufyān saw that they would not obey him, he departed for Medina and remained there.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن جبير بن عمرو بن سعيد بن ذاخر أبو سالم الجيشاني حليف معافر نزل مصر قال بن منده اختلف في صحبته قلت اتفق البخاري ومسلم وأبو حاتم والعجلي وابن حبان على أنه تابعي وقال بن يونس شهد فتح مصر وله رواية عن علي وكان قد وفد عليه وصحبه وروى أيضا عن أبي ذر وعقبة بن عامر وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص وغيرهم وروى عنه ابنه سالم وحفيده سعيد بن سالم ويزيد بن أبي حبيب وبكر بن سوادة وآخرون قال بن يونس مات بالإسكندرية في إمرة عبد العزيز بن مروان
records.english: ibn Jubayr ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn Dhākhir, Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī, an ally of Maʿāfir, settled in Egypt. Ibn Mandah said that there was disagreement over whether he had companionship. I say: Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Ḥātim, al-ʿIjlī, and Ibn Ḥibbān agreed that he was a Successor. Ibn Yūnus said that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt and related from ʿAlī, to whom he had come in a delegation and whom he accompanied. He also related from Abū Dharr, ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and others. His son Sālim, his grandson Saʿīd ibn Sālim, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, Bakr ibn Sawādah, and others related from him. Ibn Yūnus said that he died in Alexandria during the governorship of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān.

names.arabic: سفيان بن هانئ بن جبير بن عمرو بن سعيد بن ذاخر أبو سالم الجيشاني
names.english: Sufyān ibn Hāniʾ ibn Jubayr ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn Dhākhir, Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī

names.arabic: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
names.english: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الهذلي والد النضر له إدراك أخرج أبو نعيم في الدلائل من طريق النضر بن سفيان عن أبيه قال خرجنا في عير لنا إلى الشام فلما كنا بقرب معاوية عرسنا فإذا بفارس يقول وهو بين السماء والأرض أيها الناس هبوا فليس ذابحين رقاد فقد خرج أحمد وطردت الشياطين كل مطرد فرجعنا إلى أهلنا فإذا هم يذكرون أن نبيا اسمه أحمد خرج من قريش بمكة قلت وقد أخرجه الواقدي من طريق مسلم بن جندب عن النضر به
records.english: al-Hudhalī, the father of al-Naḍr. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted in al-Dalāʾil through al-Naḍr ibn Sufyān, from his father, who said: ‘We set out in a caravan of ours for Syria. When we were near Muʿāwiyah, we stopped for the night. Suddenly a horseman between heaven and earth was saying, “People, arise! This is no time for sleep. Aḥmad has emerged, and the devils have been driven away in every direction.” We returned to our people and found them saying that a prophet named Aḥmad had emerged from Quraysh in Mecca.’ I say: Al-Wāqidī also transmitted it by way of Muslim ibn Jundab, from al-Naḍr, from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بن كنيف بن سنان بن بدر بن ثعلبة بن حبال بن نصر بن غاضرة الأسدي أسد خزيمة ذكره المرزباني وقال كان في جيش خالد بن الوليد باليمامة وقال في ذلك
إني وناقتي الخوصاء مختلف
منا الهوى إذ بلغنا مدفع البين
records.english:
ibn Kunayf ibn Sinān ibn Badr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥibāl ibn Naṣr ibn Ghāḍirah al-Asadī, of Asad Khuzaymah. Al-Marzubānī mentioned him and said that he was in Khālid ibn al-Walīd's army at al-Yamāmah. He said concerning that:

My hollow-eyed she-camel and I differ in desire,
now that we have reached the place where separation begins.

names.arabic: سلمة بن حبيش بن كنيف بن سنان بن بدر بن ثعلبة بن حبال بن نصر بن غاضرة الأسدي
names.english: Salamah ibn Ḥubaysh ibn Kunayf ibn Sinān ibn Badr ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥibāl ibn Naṣr ibn Ghāḍirah al-Asadī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك وسمع من عمر ومعاذ وسلمان روى عنه أبو وائل وروى مسدد والبغوي في الجعديات من طريق أبي وائل عن سلمة بن سبرة قال خطبنا معاذ بن جبل فذكر قصة وذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي أهل الكوفة
records.english: He lived to the beginning of Islam and heard from ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and Salmān. Abū Wāʾil transmitted from him. Musaddad and al-Baghawī related in al-Jaʿdiyyāt, by way of Abū Wāʾil, from Salamah ibn Sabrah, who said: ‘Muʿādh ibn Jabal addressed us,’ and he related an account. Ibn Saʿd placed him in the first generation of the Successors of Kufa.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجهني قال بن عساكر له إدراك وجاهد بالشام فاستشهد بمرج الصفر سنة ثلاث عشرة ثم أسند ذلك عن أبي حسان الزيادي
records.english: al-Juhanī. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he lived to the beginning of Islam, fought in al-Shām, and was martyred. This occurred at Marj al-Ṣuffar in the year 13. He then transmitted that from Abū Ḥassān al-Ziyādī.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك وشهد وقعة جلولاء فروى الثوري عن راشد بن سعد قال قال السليك الفزاري لما بعث سعد بن أبي وقاص إلى جلولاء كنت فيهم ذكره بن أبي حاتم وهذا غير السليك بن سلكة التميمي أحد صعاليك العرب المشهورين مات في الجاهلية
records.english: He lived to the beginning of Islam and witnessed the battle of Jalūlāʾ. Al-Thawrī transmitted from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, who said: Sulayk al-Fazārī said, ‘When Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ dispatched men to Jalūlāʾ, I was among them.’ Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him. He is not Sulayk ibn al-Sulakah al-Tamīmī, one of the famous brigand-poets of the Arabs, who died in the pre-Islamic period.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
الأقطع له إدراك وشهد اليمامة فقطعت كفه في قتال أهل الردة وفي ذلك يقول
كيف تراني وأخي عطاردا
نذود من حنيفة المذاودا
أنشد كفا ذهبت وساعدا
أنشدها ولا أراني واجدا في أبيات
records.english:
the man with the severed hand. He lived to the beginning of Islam and witnessed al-Yamāmah, where his hand was severed while fighting the people of the apostasy. About that he said:

How do you see me and my brother ʿUṭārid,
driving the defenders of Ḥanīfah away?
I seek a hand and forearm that are gone;
I seek them, yet do not see that I shall find them.

These lines come from a longer poem.

names.english: Sulayk al-ʿUqaylī the man with the severed hand

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن المعلى الطائي ثم السنبسي له إدراك وشهد فتوح العراق فغرق يوم عبر المسلمون إلى المدائن في دلجة لم يغرق غيره ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn al-Muʿallā al-Ṭāʾī, then al-Sinbisī. He lived to the beginning of Islam and witnessed the conquests of Iraq. He drowned during a night crossing when the Muslims crossed to al-Madāʾin; no one else drowned. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him.

names.arabic: سليل بن زيد بن مالك بن المعلى الطائي ثم السنبسي
names.english: Salīl ibn Zayd ibn Mālik ibn al-Muʿallā al-Ṭāʾī, then al-Sinbisī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بكسر المهملة وسكون المثناة بن سلمة بن مالك التجيبي أبو سلمة له إدراك وشهد فتح مصر قاله سعيد بن عفير وشهد خطبة عمر بالجابية روى ذلك بن عائذ من طريق بكر بن سوادة عن عبد الرحمن بن رافع عنه وسمع أبا الدرداء قاله البخاري في التاريخ وكان يقال له الناسك لكثرة عبادته قاله بن يونس وروى بن أبي حاتم من طريق كعب بن علقمة قال كان سليم بن عتر من خير التابعين قال بن يونس كان قد هاجر في خلافة عمر وشهد خطبته بالجابية وجمع له معاوية القضاء والقصص بمصر وكانت ولايته على القضاء سنة أربعين ومات بدمياط سنة خمس وسبعين وسيأتي له ذكر في ترجمة صلة بن الحارث الغفاري وقال عبد الرحمن بن زياد بن أنعم عن عبد الرحمن بن رافع عن سليم بن عتر سجد بنا عمر في الحج سجدتين وقال بن لهيعة عن الحارث بن يزيد قلت لحنش بن عبد الله قوله تعالى كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون قال هذه والله صفة سليم بن عتر وأبي عبد الرحمن الجبلي وقال بن لهيعة عن الحارث بن يزيد كان يختم كل ثلاثة وقيل أنه كان يكثر الصلاة بالليل والجماع فلما مات قالت امرأته رحمك الله كنت ترضي ربك وتسر أهلك أخرجها أبو عبيد في فضائل القرآن وقد استوفيت اخباره في كتاب قضاة مصر
records.english: with kasrah on the undotted initial letter and sukūn on the tāʾ; ibn Salamah ibn Mālik al-Tujībī, Abū Salamah, lived into Islam and witnessed the conquest of Egypt, according to Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr. He also witnessed ʿUmar's address at al-Jābiyah. Ibn ʿĀʾidh related that by way of Bakr ibn Sawādah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ, from him. He heard Abū al-Dardāʾ, according to al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh. He was called ‘the ascetic’ because of his abundant worship, according to Ibn Yūnus. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related by way of Kaʿb ibn ʿAlqamah, who said: ‘Sulaym ibn ʿItr was among the best of the Successors.’ Ibn Yūnus said: He migrated during ʿUmar's caliphate and witnessed his address at al-Jābiyah. Muʿāwiyah combined for him the offices of judge and public admonisher in Egypt. He was appointed judge in the year 40 and died at Damietta in the year 75. He will be mentioned again in the entry on Ṣilah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ghifārī. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ, from Sulaym ibn ʿItr: ‘ʿUmar led us in making two prostrations in al-Ḥajj.’ Ibn Lahīʿah related from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd: ‘I asked Ḥanash ibn ʿAbd Allāh about the Most High's words, “They used to sleep but little of the night.” He replied, “By God, this is the description of Sulaym ibn ʿItr and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jabalī.”’ Ibn Lahīʿah also related from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd that he used to complete the Qur'an every three nights. It is said that he engaged abundantly in prayer by night and in marital relations. When he died, his wife said, ‘رحمك الله. You used to please your Lord and delight your family.’ Abū ʿUbayd transmitted this in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān. I have treated his reports comprehensively in Kitāb Quḍāt Miṣr.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن زياد بن أنعم
names.english: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿum

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري أو المخزومي مولاهم أبو عامر له إدراك قال بن خيثمة وأبو زرعة الدمشقي وأبو حاتم الرازي صلى خلف أبي بكر وقال أبو عمر سليم بن عامر وأبو عامر وليس بالخبائري وروى الطبراني في مسند الشاميين من طريق ثابت بن عجلان عن سليم أبي عامر وكان ممن سباه خالد بن الوليد حين حاصر حلب قال فلما قدمنا على أبي بكر جعلني في المكتب وعن سليم قال رأيت أبا بكر وعمر وعثمان أكلوا مما مست النار ثم صلوا ولم يتوضئوا وروى دحيم من طريق ثابت بن عجلان عنه قال صليت خلف أبي بكر سبعة أشهر وأخرجه البخاري في تاريخه الصغير وزاد وكان أبو بكر أخدمه عمار بن ياسر وكان ممن أفاء الله على خالد بن الوليد ثم شهد فتح دمشق والقادسية وقال أبو بكر البغدادي في تاريخ الحمصيين سباه خالد بن الوليد حين حاصر حلب
records.english: al-Anṣārī or al-Makhzūmī, their client, Abū ʿĀmir. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Ibn Khaythamah said, together with Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī and Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, that he prayed behind Abū Bakr. Abū ʿUmar said: ‘Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿĀmir; he is not al-Khabāʾirī.’ Al-Ṭabarānī related in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn, by way of Thābit ibn ʿAjlān, from Sulaym Abū ʿĀmir, who was among those whom Khālid ibn al-Walīd took captive when he besieged Aleppo. He said: ‘When we were brought before Abū Bakr, he placed me in the school.’ Sulaym also said: ‘I saw Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān eat food touched by fire, then pray without performing ablution.’ Duḥaym related by way of Thābit ibn ʿAjlān, from him, that he said: ‘I prayed behind Abū Bakr for seven months.’ Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his al-Tārīkh al-Ṣaghīr and added: Abū Bakr assigned ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir to serve him. He was among those whom God granted as booty to Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and he later witnessed the conquests of Damascus and al-Qādisiyyah. Abū Bakr al-Baghdādī said in Tārīkh al-Ḥimṣiyyīn that Khālid ibn al-Walīd took him captive when he besieged Aleppo.

names.arabic: سليم الأنصاري أو المخزومي مولاهم أبو عامر
names.english: Sulaym al-Anṣārī or al-Makhzūmī, their client, Abū ʿĀmir

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك وشهد يوم جلولاء وله رواية عن علي روى عنه أبو إسحاق السبيعي ذكره بن أبي حاتم وابن حبان
records.english: He lived to the beginning of Islam and witnessed the day of Jalūlāʾ. He has a narration from ʿAlī, and a transmitter reported from him—namely, Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī. Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الكندي والد شرحبيل ذكر سيف في الفتوح أنه شهد اليرموك وذكر في الردة أنه ثبت هو وولده شرحبيل على الإسلام لما ارتدت كندة وانضما إلى زياد بن لبيد لكن رأيت في التاريخ للمظفري في ذكر ردة أهل اليمن وارتدت كندة كلها الا شرحبيل بن السمط وابنه والله أعلم ثم تبين لي أن الصواب الأول وسأذكره في ترجمة شرحبيل وأورد البيهقي في السنن بسند له إلى الشعبي أن عمر استعمل شرحبيل بن السمط على المدائن وأبوه بالشام فكتب إلى عمر أنك تأمر ألا تفرق السبايا وقد فرقت بيني وبين ابني فكتب إليه فألحقه بابنه
records.english: al-Kindī, the father of Shuraḥbīl. Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that he witnessed al-Yarmūk, and in al-Riddah that he and his son Shuraḥbīl remained steadfast in Islam when Kindah apostatized and joined Ziyād ibn Labīd. Yet I saw in al-Muẓaffarī's Tārīkh, in the account of the apostasy of the people of Yemen: ‘All of Kindah apostatized except Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ and his son.’ والله أعلم I then became certain that the former version is correct. I shall explain it in the entry on Shuraḥbīl. Al-Bayhaqī cited in al-Sunan, with a chain of his to al-Shaʿbī, that ʿUmar appointed Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ governor of al-Madāʾin while his father was in Syria. His father wrote to ʿUmar: ‘You command that female captives not be separated, yet you have separated me from my son.’ ʿUmar wrote back ordering him to join his son.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بن مساحق بن بجير بن أسامة بن نصر بن قعين بن الحارث بن ثعلبة بن دودان بن أسد بن خزيمة الأسدي أبو السمال آخره لام والميم مشددة الشاعر له إدراك ونزل الكوفة قال أبو حاتم السجستاني في المعمرين حدثنا مشيختنا أن سمعان بن هبيرة هو أبو السمال الأسدي عاش مائة وسبعا وستين سنة وقال الدارقطني في المؤتلف كان مع طليحة في الردة فلما دهمهم خالد قال لطليحة بم أمرت فذكر القصة وقال الزبير بن بكار في كتاب النسب حدثني عمر بن أبي بكر الموصلي عن أبي صالح الفقعي وأبي فقعس الأسديين وكان من علماء العرب قال ولد أسد بن خزيمة عمرا فولد عمرو لخما وجذيمة وعاملة وفي ذلك يقول أبو السمال سمعان بن هبيرة وساق نسبه كالذي هنا الأسدي
أبلغ جذاما ولخما معا
على اليعملات أولات الحقيب
وقولا لعاملة الأقربين
كأن أولئك أولي نسيب
قبائل منا يأت دارهم
وهم في القرابة أدنى قريب
هلموا إلينا نخلو إلى
أخ معتف ومحل رحيب وقال مغيرة بن مقسم كان أبو السمال لا يغلق باب داره وكان له مناد ينادي من ليس له خطة فمنزله على أبي السمال قال فبلغ ذلك عثمان فاتخذ دارا لأضيافه وقال المرزباني في معجمه هو الذي شرب في رمضان مع النجاشي الحارثي فأقام الحد على النجاشي وهرب أبو السمال وأنشد له في ذلك شعرا قاله
records.english:
ibn Musāḥiq ibn Bujayr ibn Usāmah ibn Naṣr ibn Quʿayn ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Dūdān ibn Asad ibn Khuzaymah al-Asadī, Abū al-Sammāl—ending in lām, with the mīm doubled—the poet, lived into Islam and settled in Kufa. Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī said in al-Muʿammarīn: ‘Our shaykhs related to us that Samʿān ibn Hubayrah was Abū al-Sammāl al-Asadī and that he lived 167 years.’ Al-Dāraquṭnī said in al-Muʾtalif: ‘He was with Ṭulayḥah during the apostasy. When Khālid descended upon them, he asked Ṭulayḥah, “What have you been commanded?”’ and he related the story. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said in Kitāb al-Nasab: ‘ʿUmar ibn Abī Bakr al-Mawṣilī related to me, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Faqʿī and Abū Faqʿas al-Asadī, the latter one of the scholars of the Arabs, who said: Asad ibn Khuzaymah fathered ʿAmr; ʿAmr fathered Lakhm, Judhāmah, and ʿĀmilah.’ Abū al-Sammāl Samʿān ibn Hubayrah said concerning this, and al-Zubayr gave his lineage as it appears here, al-Asadī:

Convey to Judhām and Lakhm together,
upon sturdy camels bearing saddle packs,
and say to our nearest kin of ʿĀmilah:
as though those were the people of lineage.
Tribes sprung from us, though their homes lie far,
while in kinship they are our nearest relatives.
Come to us, that we may retire together
to a brother who shelters guests and a spacious dwelling.

Mughīrah ibn Miqsam said that Abū al-Sammāl never closed the door of his house. He had a caller proclaim, ‘Whoever has no allotted dwelling, his lodging is with Abū al-Sammāl.’ News of that reached ʿUthmān, so he established a house for his guests. Al-Marzubānī said in his Muʿjam that he was the man who drank wine in Ramadan with al-Najāshī al-Ḥārithī. The prescribed punishment was carried out upon al-Najāshī, while Abū al-Sammāl fled. Al-Marzubānī cited poetry of his concerning this.

names.arabic: سمعان بن هبيرة بن مساحق بن بجير بن أسامة بن نصر بن قعين بن الحارث بن ثعلبة بن دودان بن أسد بن خزيمة الأسدي أبو السمال
names.english: Samʿān ibn Hubayrah ibn Musāḥiq ibn Bujayr ibn Usāmah ibn Naṣr ibn Quʿayn ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Dūdān ibn Asad ibn Khuzaymah al-Asadī, Abū al-Sammāl

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن نهار بن غانم بن سعد بن جبل بن كنانة بن ناجية بن مراد المرادي له إدراك وله بن يقال له زائدة قتل مع علي بالنهروان ذكره بن الكلبي وسيأتي ذكر أخيه عمرو بن عبد الله بن نهار
records.english: ibn Nahār ibn Ghānim ibn Saʿd ibn Jabal ibn Kinānah ibn Nājiyah ibn Murād al-Murādī lived into Islam. He had a son called Zāʾidah who was killed fighting alongside ʿAlī at al-Nahrawān. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him. His brother ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nahār will be mentioned later.

names.arabic: سمير بن عبد الله بن نهار بن غانم بن سعد بن جبل بن كنانة بن ناجية بن مراد المرادي
names.english: Sumayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nahār ibn Ghānim ibn Saʿd ibn Jabal ibn Kinānah ibn Nājiyah ibn Murād al-Murādī

names.arabic: عمرو بن عبد الله بن نهار
names.english: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nahār

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك وكتب إلى عمر في وقعة جرت له وله رواية عن عمران بن حصين وعنه عمران بن حدير وعاصم الأحول وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين
records.english: He lived to the beginning of Islam and wrote to ʿUmar about an incident that befell him. He also has a narration from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, while ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr and ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal related from him. Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the trustworthy Successors.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وبالفاء والسمفعة الأقدام والجرأة قاله بن دريد ووهم من ضبطه بالقاف وكذا من ضم أوله فصيره مصغرا تقدم في ذي الكلاع
records.english: with fatḥah on its first letter and with fāʾ. Al-samfaʿah means boldness and courage; Ibn Durayd said this. Whoever vocalized it with qāf erred, as did whoever gave the first letter ḍamma and made it a diminutive. He appeared earlier under Dhū al-Kalāʿ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وتخفيف النون وبعد الألف مهملة يقال هو اسم أبي صفرة والد المهلب
records.english: with fatḥah on its first letter, an ungeminated nūn, and an undotted letter after the alif. It is said to be the name of Abū Ṣufrah. Abū Ṣufrah was the father of al-Muhallab.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الوداعي له إدراك أخرج الدارقطني في السنن من طريق صفوان بن سليم عن سعيد بن المسيب قال لما حج عمر حجته الأخيرة غودر رجل من المسلمين قتيلا في بني وداعة فبعث إليهم عمر فسألهم فقالوا لا نعلم من قتله فأمر فاستخرج منهم خمسون شيخا فأدخلهم الحطيم واستحلفهم بالله رب هذا البيت الحرام والبلد الحرام والمشعر الحرام إنهم لم يقتلوه ولا علموا له قاتلا فحلفوا بذلك فقال أدوا ديته فقال رجل منهم يقال له سنان ما تجزيني يميني من مالي قال لا إنما قضيت فيكم بقضاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي سنده عمر بن صبح وهو متروك
records.english: al-Wadāʿī. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted in al-Sunan through Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When ʿUmar made his final pilgrimage, a Muslim man was left slain among the Banū Wadāʿah. ʿUmar sent for them and questioned them. They replied that they did not know who had killed him. He ordered fifty of their elders brought out and admitted them into al-Ḥaṭīm. He made them swear by God—the Lord of this Sacred House, the Sacred City, and the Sacred Monument—that they had not killed him and did not know his killer. They so swore, whereupon he said, ‘Pay his blood money.’ A man among them called Sinān said, ‘Does my oath not protect my wealth?’ He replied, ‘No. I have only judged you by the judgment of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم.’ In its chain is ʿUmar ibn Ṣubḥ, who is abandoned.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن الصحبان بن الحارث بن عمرو بن عدي الأزدي له إدراك وكان ولده عبد الله من الفرسان الشجعان وكان مع المهلب فكان المهلب يقول ما وقعت في عظيمة قط فرأيت عبد الله بن سنان الا أفرخ روعي ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn al-Ṣaḥbān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī al-Azdī. He had lived into Islam. His son ʿAbd Allāh was one of the courageous horsemen and served with al-Muhallab. Al-Muhallab used to say, ‘Never did I fall into a grave danger and then see ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān without my fear subsiding.’ Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him.

names.arabic: سنان بن كعب بن مالك بن الصحبان بن الحارث بن عمرو بن عدي الأزدي
names.english: Sinān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik ibn al-Ṣaḥbān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī al-Azdī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن خاقان بن خويلد بن حرثان الغنوي قال المرزباني شاعر شامي مخضرم وأنشد له بيتا قاله من أبيات
records.english: ibn Khāqān ibn Khuwaylid ibn Ḥarthān al-Ghanawī. Al-Marzubānī said: a poet from Syria who lived across the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. He cited one line of his from a longer poem.

names.arabic: سهم بن حنظلة بن خاقان بن خويلد بن حرثان الغنوي
names.english: Sahm ibn Ḥanẓalah ibn Khāqān ibn Khuwaylid ibn Ḥarthān al-Ghanawī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن هزمة بسكون الزاي ويقال جرم له إدراك قاله بن عساكر قال وشهد فتح دمشق وروى من طريق سيف بن عمر عن خالد وعبادة قال وبقي مع يزيد بن أبي سفيان بعد اليرموك من أهل اليمن عدد منهم سهم بن المسافر بن هرمة
records.english: ibn Hazmah, with sukūn on the zāy; he is also said to be Jurm. He lived to the beginning of Islam. Ibn … said this—that is, Ibn ʿAsākir, who stated that Sahm witnessed the conquest of Damascus. He related by way of Sayf ibn ʿUmar, from Khālid and ʿUbādah: After al-Yarmūk, a number of Yemenites remained with Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān, including Sahm ibn al-Musāfir ibn Harmah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ينظر مسند الحارث بن معاوية ويحرر من النسب وغيره
records.english: Consult the musnad of al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah, and verify the lineage and other details.
